text:
Evan Brooks: Heads-up: launching a Docs Signed Snippet policy today. Goal: every canonical snippet must carry a checksum + signer metadata so we can prove provenance and roll back bad copy-paste more easily. Preview doc: https://docs.redwood/preview/signed-snippets
Sana Ali: Can you explain the signer metadata? Who signs and where is the checksum stored?
Evan Brooks: Short version: author commits snippet canonical file; CI generates a SHA256 checksum and records signer (GitHub username + commit SHA) in a small metadata registry file stored alongside the snippet. Example metadata line: `id: sdk_python_quickstart_call; checksum: sha256:abcd...; signed_by: sana.ali; signed_at: 2098765432`
Tim Reynolds: Does this change copying snippets into SDK examples or marketing pages?
Evan Brooks: Copy-paste remains unchanged for users. Internally, we require editors to reference the canonical id or include the metadata header if they paste a snippet. The linter will warn if a snippet lacks a matching checksum entry.
Maya Fernandez: Docs action items? I can add the policy page and a migration checklist for authors. Also will add a small authoring UX note for Solutions and PMs.
Evan Brooks: Thanks. Key enforcement points: 1) `snippet-sign` CI job runs on PRs and will attach `signed-snippet` badge when checksum matches; 2) After a 45-day grace period, `snippet-lint` will fail PRs that add new canonical snippets without signer metadata.
DocsBot: Preview for the signer workflow: https://docs.redwood/preview/signed-snippets-workflow. The badge mockup is here: https://assets.redwood/badges/signed-snippet.svg
Sana Ali: What about previously accepted snippets? Will we need to backfill metadata for hundreds of small examples?
Evan Brooks: We'll provide an automated backfill script that heuristically matches snippets to canonical ids and generates metadata PRs for authors to review. Backfill plan: automated PRs first, maintainers approve or reassign within 14 days. If no response, maintainers will be nudged by the `docs-automation` bot.
Tim Reynolds: Any legal/IP implications? We should make sure the signature model doesn't imply code ownership change. @LegalBot please advise on wording for policy.
LegalBot: Reviewed at a high level. Draft language should clarify that signing asserts provenance (author+commit), not transfer of rights. Recommend a short clause in the policy and a checkbox for authors during signing that says "I confirm this snippet is original or properly licensed." I'll post suggested text by EOD.
Maya Fernandez: CI details for DevEx? We need a small action that computes checksum and updates registry. Also a UI hint in the docs editor to show whether a snippet is signed.
DevExBot: `snippet-sign` GitHub Action added to `devex/actions`. It computes `sha256` for the code block, writes to `snippets/registry.csv`, and opens a PR with the updated registry if run on a fork. We also added `snippet-badge` job to the site build to render the signed badge inline when registry entry exists.
Sana Ali: Rollout timeline and rollback plan?
Evan Brooks: Timeline: preview today; automated backfill + registry PRs over 2 weeks; opt-in enforcement (linter warnings) for 45 days; enforcement (CI failure) after 45 days. Rollback: if backfill causes mass conflicts, we can revert the registry commits and pause enforcement while we triage.
Tim Reynolds: How do we handle third-party contributed snippets from partners or open-source repos?
Evan Brooks: Partners must sign snippets via the same PR flow (we'll accept signed registry entries from external contributors). For external repos we can add a verification step: `verify-external-snippet` job that ensures the snippet matches the published canonical content.
Maya Fernandez: I'll draft the migration checklist (approve backfill PRs, run local sign script, update examples) and add a short FAQ for Solutions with suggested timelines for customers who embed snippets in public docs.
DocsBot: Reminder: label preview issues `signed-snippets-preview` and tag @Maya Fernandez. Also note the preview contains example registry and a demo PR.
Evan Brooks: Final asks: Legal to post the wording; DevEx to finalize the Action and a dry-run mode; Maya to publish the policy page and checklist. We'll reconvene at the end of the 2-week backfill window. Thanks all.
